subject: Capacity runway & renewal review — usage diagnostics + expansion options
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@zephyr.ai>, Tim Hsu <tim.hsu@zephyr.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity runway & renewal review — usage diagnostics + expansion options

Hi Maya / Tim,

Following up with a short readout from our usage analysis ahead of your renewal conversation. I pulled the last 90 days of token spend and latency profiles and attached two quick artifacts: zephyr_usage_snapshot_q3.csv and latency_report_nov.pdf. Top-level findings: 

- Baseline (P95 throughput): ~650k tokens/day with steady weekday peaks ~950k tokens/day.
- Burst events: three multi-hour spikes correlated with new feature rollouts on 10/12, 10/28, and 11/08. These drove a ~2.2x marginal cost for those days.
- Latency: average 180ms, tails (99th) hit ~600ms during the largest bursts.
- ROI signal: your primary user journeys (search-autocomplete & reply generation) show ~28% fewer downstream API calls when we enable prefix caching — this maps to ~13% token savings on those flows.

Given the usage shape, two directions seem reasonable for the renewal:
1) 12-month committed capacity sized ~1.5–2x current baseline (best unit economics + predictable cost)
2) 6–9 month flexible commit with burst credits + reserved buffer for known launch windows

I'd like to schedule a 30-minute renewal health review next week to walk through the numbers and the recommended pricing shapes. Are you available Wed 11/25 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 11/26 11:00–11:30 PT?

Next steps I propose for the meeting: quick usage walk, proposed commitment tiers (with cost/ROI), and an implementation plan for KV/prefix caching to reduce marginal token spend during bursts.

Thanks — I'll loop in Lauren and Ben to prepare a short pricing sketch.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: zephyr_usage_snapshot_q3.csv, latency_report_nov.pdf
From: Maya Patel <maya@zephyr.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity runway & renewal review — usage diagnostics + expansion options

Connor — thanks for the summary and the files. Helpful.

A couple of quick notes before the meeting:
- We're leaning toward a longer-term commit (12 months) if the economics and step-up plan make sense — our upcoming product releases in Jan/Feb will increase average session length and we need runway.
- Can you include a line-item showing the cost delta if we enable full prefix/KV caching vs current? We want to understand the implementation lift vs savings.
- Procurement (procurement@zephyr.ai) is copied — they want to see a short summary and a draft amendment if we move forward.

I've attached a small forecast (zephyr_forecast_q4.xlsx) showing our expected token trajectory per sprint; it's conservative but shows a potential 1.8x baseline by end of Q1.

We can do Wed 11/25 10:00 PT.

— Maya
Maya Patel
VP Product, Zephyr Labs
maya@zephyr.ai

Attachments: zephyr_forecast_q4.xlsx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Capacity runway & renewal review — prep notes from Zephyr (internal)

Lauren / Ben — forwarding Maya's reply + forecast. Key asks: 12mo headline looks likely, and procurement wants amendment + a clear cost/ROI on prefix/KV caching. Meeting confirmed Wed 11/25 10:00 PT.

Proposal sketch (high level):
- Option A (Committed 12mo): 1.75x baseline reserved tokens + 20% burst buffer, monthly invoiced. Estimated unit cost: $0.0042/token equivalent (post-commit).
- Option B (Step-up hybrid 9mo): 9mo term with tiered step-ups at months 3 and 6, burst credits for scheduled launches. Estimated blended unit: $0.0049/token.
- Implementation work: enable prefix/KV caching on their highest-volume routes (search & reply gen). Expected token savings 10–18% depending on coverage. One-time infra setup and tuning estimated 2–3 engineer days from our side.

Can you draft a short ROI calc (3-line table) that I can share in the meeting and a pricing_breakdown we can send to procurement if they push? I've started a short outline in proposal_sketch.txt (attached).

Thanks — I want to make the 12mo the default ask but have the step-up hybrid as fallback.

Connor

Attachments: proposal_sketch.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Capacity runway & renewal review — prep notes from Zephyr (internal)

Connor / Lauren — here's a concise pricing break to bring to the call; I attached pricing_breakdown.xlsx with line items. Executive summary:

- Recommended commercial: 12-month commitment at 1.6x baseline with a 12% unit discount vs pay-as-you-go. Include 15% burst credits for scheduled launches (two per quarter).
- Alternative (win-back): 9-month hybrid with an auto step-up to 1.4x at month 3 and 1.6x at month 6; include overage credits for first 60 days post-launch.
- Amendments: standard renewal amendment + SOW clause for caching implementation (2–3 eng days) and a performance SLA for P95 latency under committed capacity.

Operational notes to call out in the meeting: enabling KV/prefix caching will likely drop peak marginal spend by ~14% on search flows and reduce P99 tail by ~120–180ms on heavy bursts. If they provision Dedicated pools we can set autoscaling headroom and reserve a fallback model variant in a cheaper quantized profile for overflow.

I attached a quick price model and sample amendment language in pricing_breakdown.xlsx. If procurement asks for faster legal turnaround, we can include a pre-approved amendment template.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: pricing_breakdown.xlsx

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity runway & renewal review — usage diagnostics + expansion options

Connor / Ben / Lauren — thanks for the walkthrough earlier and for the pricing materials. After reviewing internally with product and procurement, Zephyr is prepared to proceed with the 12-month committed option with a staged step-up: 1.25x baseline for months 1–3, 1.6x baseline months 4–12, and a 15% burst credit pool for scheduled launches. Procurement asked for a draft amendment and a DocuSign-ready agreement we can sign next week.

Two asks before we finalize:
1) Can you include the expected token savings scenario if we enable full prefix/KV caching on search & reply routes (best / base / conservative)? Ben suggested ~10–18% — procurement wants a short table.
2) Please include the SLA commitment for P95 latency under committed capacity and the fallback policy (which model variant we fall back to, and whether fallbacks are quantized).

If you can send a short amendment + DocuSign link, procurement will prioritize and we should be able to close by EOD Friday.

I'll attach the signed internal approval once they route it.

Best,
Maya Patel
VP Product, Zephyr Labs

Attachments: amendment_request_notes.txt, expected_signoff_timeline.txt
